nouns.explanation: The room in which a person sleeps.
The piece of furniture that you sleep on.
Two beds, one fixed above the other.
The thick, soft part of a bed that you lie on.
Soft cushions for the head.
A thick, soft bed covering filled with feathers or fibre.
A warm bed cover made of layers of cloth stitched together.
A warm covering for a bed.
The sheets and blankets on a bed.
A tall cupboard for hanging clothes in.
A piece of furniture with drawers for clothes.
A small table next to a bed.
A small, dim light left on during the night.
Flat boards fixed to a wall for holding things.
Lengths of cloth that hang across a window.
An opening in a wall, filled with glass, that lets in light.
The long planks that make up a floor.
Patterned paper pasted onto walls.
Large printed pictures fixed to a wall.
Magazines that tell stories in pictures.
A soft toy bear.
The things that people wear.
A clock that rings to wake you.
The room at the very top of a house, under the roof.
A bedroom for a baby or very young child.
The light of the moon.
The places where two walls meet.
The upper surface of a room.
The pipe that carries smoke up through the roof.
The special clothes worn by everyone at a school.

adjectives.explanation: Soft and fluffy, like the feathers of a young bird.
Made of many small pieces of cloth sewn together.
In a state of complete mess and confusion.
Full of things in an untidy way.
Higher on one side than the other.
Made of a thick, very soft cloth.
Made from the strong wood of the oak tree.
Old, shaky and likely to break.
Full of fresh air and space.
Worn so thin that the threads show.

verbs.explanation: Settled into a warm, comfortable position.
Bent the body into a rounded shape.
Moved restlessly from side to side.
Dropped down heavily and loosely.
Jumped up and down.
Poured in, like light or water.
Filled a place completely.
Made the regular sound of a clock.
Shone with a soft light.
Made a long, squeaking sound.
Lay scattered untidily over a place.
Covered a surface thickly.
Was fixed at the top and reached down.
Shook something so that it made quick knocking sounds.
Made a long, low sound.
Filled with air and swelled outwards.
Opened the mouth wide from tiredness.
Reached out the arms and legs.
Moved slowly and gently. To drift off is to fall asleep.
Stopped sleeping.
Moved slowly and quietly.
Heaped up.
Rested flat.
Pushed in quickly and carelessly.
Walked very quietly on the toes.
Dug down into something for warmth or shelter.
Pulled something along.
Bent downwards in the middle.
Pulled back suddenly from something unpleasant.
Moved fast through the air.

sentences.text: She snuggled under the covers in her warm, cosy bedroom while the rain drummed on the roof.
He curled up with a book against the soft, downy pillows.
All night she tossed and turned on the narrow, lumpy bed.
He flopped onto the bed and dragged the thick, patchwork quilt over his head.
The twins bounced on the mattress until the rickety bunk beds shook.
Morning sunshine streamed through the curtains and flooded the bright, airy bedroom.
An alarm clock ticked on the bedside table, far too loudly.
A night light glowed beside the bed, holding the dark at bay.
The tall, oak wardrobe creaked in the night as though something inside had shifted.
Toys and comics littered the floor of the chaotic, cluttered bedroom.
His school uniform hung in the wardrobe, pressed and waiting.
The wind rattled the window and moaned in the chimney.
White curtains billowed in the breeze like sails.
Heavy, velvet curtains shut out the street lamps.
He yawned and stretched, then burrowed back beneath the snug, feather-filled duvet.
Listening to the rain, she drifted off to sleep.
He woke with a start, certain that someone had spoken his name.
Strange shapes crept across the ceiling, and the dark, shadowy corners seemed to breathe.
A crumpled heap of clothes lay on the floor, and more were piled on the chair.
Posters of footballers plastered the walls.
She lay wide awake, listening to the footsteps on the stairs.
Everything he could not be bothered to tidy was stuffed under the bed.
She tiptoed to the window, her feet flinching from the cold, bare floorboards.
Pale, silver moonlight lay across the bed like a second sheet.
The tiny, sloping attic room had space for a bed, a chest of drawers and very little else.
The spartan, chilly room held nothing but a bed and a broken chair.
Faded, peeling wallpaper hung from the walls of the empty nursery.
A threadbare, one-eyed teddy bear sat on the pillow, waiting for bedtime.
Dusty, crowded shelves sagged under the weight of his books.
Pillows flew across the room, and the bedroom rang with giggles.
